title: Roku’s First OLED TV Is the User-Friendly Experience You’re Looking For
gist: Wired rates Roku's first OLED, the $1,000 Pro Series (55 or 65 inch), 7/10: strong color and blacks and best-in-class software, but limited brightness, weak speakers and Wi-Fi 5.

insights.claim: Roku's first OLED starts at $1,000 (listed $900 at Amazon) in only 55 and 65 inch sizes, with a $300 Prime Day discount cited as precedent for deep cuts.
insights.speaker: Rick Broida
insights.so_what: OLED price points near $1,000 push the technology toward mainstream, pressuring mini-LED and QLED midrange.
insights.quote: Roku just entered the chat with its first-ever OLED, and it starts at a reasonable $1,000

insights.claim: The reviewer finds limited peak brightness is the main compromise, giving less 'pop' than high-end LG and Sony OLEDs, and compares it to LG's affordable B6.
insights.speaker: Rick Broida
insights.so_what: Budget OLEDs trade brightness for price, keeping a quality gap versus premium panels.
insights.quote: Colors dazzle, black levels go deep

insights.claim: Cost-cutting shows in Wi-Fi 5 instead of Wi-Fi 6, a non-rechargeable remote, and speakers that turn harsh at higher volume, worse than Roku's prior Pro Series TV.
insights.speaker: Rick Broida
insights.so_what: Spec shortfalls signal where Roku trimmed bill-of-materials on a 'Pro' product.

themes.theme: Software as differentiator and ad model

insights.claim: Roku's OS is judged the most intuitive TV interface, with ads on nearly a third of the home screen but mostly streaming-related rather than product ads as on Amazon and Google.
insights.speaker: Rick Broida
insights.so_what: Platform ad monetization is the real business of cheap TVs; Roku positions ads as less intrusive.
insights.quote: Ads do crop up in various places—nearly a third of the home screen

insights.claim: Smart Picture Max auto-detects content and disables motion smoothing for most shows, but Dolby Vision content overrides it and turns smoothing back on.
insights.speaker: Rick Broida
insights.so_what: Automated picture tuning is a usability edge over OLEDs needing manual tweaks.

insights.claim: Roku's voice control is limited to its own UI and lacks Alexa+ or Google Assistant smarts, except for Roku-branded smart-home gear.
insights.speaker: Rick Broida
insights.so_what: Roku lags in assistant-AI integration versus Amazon and Google TV competitors.
